project.name: fibcalc
project.description: A high-performance Fibonacci calculator written in Go demonstrating Clean Architecture, sync.Pool memory pooling, adaptive parallelism, and algorithmic optimizations (Fast Doubling, Matrix Exponentiation with Strassen, FFT-based multiplication via Schönhage-Strassen, GMP backend). ~35,500 LOC across 23 packages. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: bump.go
nodes.summary: BumpAllocator providing O(1) linear arena allocation for FFT temporaries with a size-classed sync.Pool for reuse and a capacity estimator for FFT working sets.
nodes.languageNotes: Critical hot-path allocator — sync.Pool is keyed by capacity class; release routing must match acquire class to avoid leaks.

nodes.name: BumpAllocator
nodes.summary: Linear bump-pointer allocator over a pre-sized []big.Word backing, with Alloc/AllocUnsafe variants and Fermat-specific helpers.

nodes.name: AcquireBumpAllocator
nodes.summary: Acquires a BumpAllocator from the size-classed sync.Pool, growing the backing slice if the requested capacity exceeds the pooled one.

nodes.name: ReleaseBumpAllocator
nodes.summary: Returns a BumpAllocator to its size-class pool after resetting the offset; release class must match acquire class.

nodes.name: EstimateBumpCapacity
nodes.summary: Estimates the required bump-arena capacity in words given the input operand size, accounting for FFT working buffers and Fermat temporaries.

nodes.name: bump_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit and benchmark coverage for BumpAllocator semantics (alloc/reset/fallback) and end-to-end perf benchmarks for FFT mul/sqr using bump arenas.

nodes.name: context.go
nodes.summary: FFTContext value-type that injects a transform-cache and tunables into FFT mul/sqr operations, providing the global-free entry points MulWithContext, SqrWithContext, and their *To variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Architectural trajectory away from package globals: caller-scoped FFTContext threads cache and bump arenas through transformWithBumpCtx and friends.

nodes.name: FFTContext
nodes.summary: Per-caller FFT execution context bundling the transform cache, parallelism config, and arena policy; resolved lazily via the resolved() method.

nodes.name: FFTContextOptions
nodes.summary: Builder options for NewFFTContext: cache enablement, cache config override, and parallelism settings.

nodes.name: NewFFTContext
nodes.summary: Constructs an FFTContext from FFTContextOptions, resolving defaults for the transform cache and parallelism config.

nodes.name: MulWithContext
nodes.summary: Allocates a fresh big.Int and computes x*y via the FFT routine governed by the supplied context.

nodes.name: MulToWithContext
nodes.summary: In-place FFT multiplication into destination z; reuses storage and honors the context-supplied cache and bump arena.

nodes.name: SqrWithContext
nodes.summary: Computes x*x via FFT squaring using context-scoped cache and arena.

nodes.name: SqrToWithContext
nodes.summary: In-place FFT squaring into destination z, mirroring MulToWithContext.

nodes.name: transformWithBumpCtx
nodes.summary: Context-aware forward FFT that allocates its temporaries from a supplied bump arena, bypassing package-global pools.

nodes.name: invTransformWithBumpCtx
nodes.summary: Context-aware inverse FFT routine with arena-backed temporaries; the symmetric counterpart to transformWithBumpCtx.

nodes.name: mulCachedWithBumpCtx
nodes.summary: Pointwise polynomial multiply consuming both operands from the transform cache and using the context bump arena for output backing.

nodes.name: sqrCachedWithBumpCtx
nodes.summary: Pointwise squaring of a cached transform with arena-backed PolValues; companion to mulCachedWithBumpCtx.

nodes.summary: Tests that FFTContext yields correct mul/sqr results, falls back to defaults when nil, isolates parallel contexts, and obeys DisableCache.

nodes.summary: Snapshot struct describing detected CPU instruction-set extensions, exposed via GetCPUFeatures and its String() formatter.

nodes.summary: Populates the package-level CPU feature flags from golang.org/x/sys/cpu; called from init().

nodes.summary: Tests the BMI2/ADX accessors and the String() formatters for CPUFeatures and SIMDLevel.

nodes.summary: Package documentation for internal/bigfft describing the Schönhage-Strassen FFT multiplication, bump allocator, and Fermat-ring arithmetic layers.

nodes.name: fermat.go

nodes.languageNotes: Invariant violations panic intentionally; the *Safe wrappers convert recovered panics into errors. CLAUDE.md warns: never wrap a global recover here.

nodes.name: Mul
nodes.summary: Computes x = x*y in the Fermat ring 2^(64*n)+1 using either schoolbook or FFT depending on size; mutates x in place.

nodes.name: Sqr
nodes.summary: Specialized squaring in the Fermat ring; saves work versus Mul(x,x) by exploiting symmetry of the basic-case product.

nodes.name: Shift
nodes.summary: Cyclic shift x << k mod 2^n+1 used as the negacyclic twiddle multiplication primitive across the FFT.

nodes.name: ShiftHalf
nodes.summary: Multiplication by a half-integer twiddle (square root of two in the Fermat ring) reused by NTransform.

nodes.name: basicMul
nodes.summary: Internal schoolbook multiplication routine used when operands are below the FFT crossover.

nodes.name: basicSqr
nodes.summary: Internal schoolbook squaring exploiting symmetric partial products for ~50% speedup over basicMul(x,x).

nodes.name: MulSafe
nodes.summary: Panic-recovering wrapper around Mul that converts invariant violations into errors for caller-side handling.

nodes.name: fermat_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests Fermat-ring Sqr against Mul, edge cases (zero, one, MaxWord), and the *Safe wrappers' error-return contract.

nodes.name: fft.go
nodes.summary: High-level FFT multiplication API: Mul/MulTo and Sqr/SqrTo on big.Int, plus FFTParams selection and the legacy global-state entry points.

nodes.name: Mul
nodes.summary: Public big.Int multiplication entry point that allocates a result and delegates to MulTo.

nodes.name: MulTo
nodes.summary: In-place big.Int multiplication that routes to FFT or falls back to math/big depending on operand size.

nodes.name: Sqr
nodes.summary: Public big.Int squaring entry point that allocates a result and delegates to SqrTo.

nodes.name: SqrTo
nodes.summary: In-place big.Int squaring delegating to sqrFFT or falling back to MulTo(x,x) for small operands.

nodes.summary: Returns the (k, m) FFT parameters used for an operand of the given word length; exposed for diagnostics and tests.

nodes.name: fftSize
nodes.summary: Picks the FFT length parameter k for multiplying x*y, balancing chunk size against transform depth.

nodes.name: valueSize
nodes.summary: Computes the per-coefficient Fermat-ring modulus size n in machine words from FFT parameters k and m.

nodes.name: fft_cache.go
nodes.summary: LRU TransformCache for memoizing forward FFT transforms keyed by operand bytes and FFT parameters; uses FNV-based key construction and provides bump-aware cached transform/mul/sqr helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: CLAUDE.md flags this as a risk area: during eviction the recycled backing can still be aliased by a live PolValues; putByKey only allocates a fresh backing when none can be recycled.

nodes.name: TransformCache
nodes.summary: Thread-safe LRU cache mapping (operand, FFT params) keys to precomputed forward-FFT polynomial values, with stats and periodic logging.

nodes.name: TransformCacheConfig
nodes.summary: Tunables for TransformCache: capacity, minimum-bits gate, stats log interval, and enable flag.

nodes.name: cacheKeyBuilder
nodes.summary: FNV-1a hash builder that folds operand words plus FFT parameters into a 64-bit cache key.

nodes.name: CacheStats
nodes.summary: Snapshot of cache counters (hits, misses, evictions, size) exposed via TransformCache.Stats().

nodes.name: Get
nodes.summary: Looks up a precomputed PolValues for the given operand bytes and FFT parameters, returning hit/miss.

nodes.name: getByKey
nodes.summary: Inner cache lookup that updates LRU recency on hit, increments stat counters, and clones the cached PolValues for caller safety.

nodes.name: Put
nodes.summary: Inserts a PolValues into the cache under a key derived from the operand bytes and FFT parameters.

nodes.name: putByKey
nodes.summary: Inner cache insertion that evicts the LRU entry, recycles its backing slice when possible, and only allocates a fresh backing when none can be reused.

nodes.name: TransformCached

nodes.name: MulCached
nodes.summary: Multiplies two Polys via the cache: looks up forward transforms, then performs pointwise mul and inverse transform.

nodes.name: MulCachedWithBump
nodes.summary: Arena-backed variant of MulCached for the bump-allocator hot path.

nodes.name: SqrCachedWithBump

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: Every fibcalc invocation starts here. main.go is a 42-line stub that constructs the Application object from internal/app and translates its returned ExitAction into a process exit code. Keeping main.go this thin is deliberate: it enforces the Clean Architecture rule that cmd/ owns nothing but process boundaries, while all wiring lives in internal/app. README.md is included alongside so you can read the project's own framing of features (Fast Doubling default, FFT, GMP, TUI) before diving deeper.
tour.languageLesson: Go's `cmd/<binary>/main.go` convention keeps each executable's entry point tiny and pushes all business logic into `internal/`. The `internal/` directory name is enforced by the compiler: packages under it cannot be imported by any module outside the parent of internal/, giving the project a hard public-API boundary for free.

tour.title: Application Lifecycle and Dispatch
tour.description: app.go is the wiring hub that main.go delegates to. Run() builds the AppConfig from flags and environment, then a dispatch loop routes execution to one of four modes: shell completion, calibration, TUI dashboard, or the default calculate command. calculate.go is the workhorse mode: it validates the memory budget, sets up timeout and signal contexts, hands control to orchestration, and presents results. This separation lets each mode reuse the same config and progress-reporting plumbing without bleeding mode-specific logic into the rest of the system.

tour.title: Orchestration Layer
tour.description: Once calculate.go has a valid config, it calls into orchestration. ExecuteCalculations in orchestrator.go runs one or more algorithms concurrently via errgroup, with a bounded semaphore so a multi-algorithm comparison never oversubscribes the CPU. interfaces.go declares the narrow boundary types (ExecutionConfig, CalculationResult, ProgressReporter, ResultPresenter, ErrorHandler) that orchestration both consumes and exposes. Everything below this layer programs against these interfaces, which is what makes the fibonacci and bigfft packages swappable and independently testable.
tour.languageLesson: Go uses structural (duck-typed) interfaces: any type with the right method set automatically satisfies an interface, no `implements` keyword required. The Interface Segregation Principle is therefore enforced socially through narrow interfaces like `ProgressReporter` and `ResultPresenter` rather than through inheritance. `golang.org/x/sync/errgroup` adds cancellation-on-first-error semantics on top of `sync.WaitGroup`, which is why orchestration uses it for concurrent algorithm runs.

tour.title: Fibonacci Domain Facade
tour.description: calculator.go defines the public FibCalculator type that orchestration consumes. It is a thin wrapper around an inner CoreCalculator strategy, layered with cross-cutting concerns the algorithms shouldn't have to know about: memory budgeting, GC control, FFT cache configuration, and progress reporting. This is the Bridge pattern in action — the public Calculator API stays stable while the underlying strategy (Fast Doubling, Matrix, FFT, GMP) is selected at runtime from config.

tour.title: Fast Doubling: The Default Algorithm
tour.description: Fast Doubling is fibcalc's default and the README's headline algorithm. It exploits the identity F(2k) = F(k)(2F(k+1) − F(k)) to compute F(n) in O(log n) big-integer multiplications. fastdoubling.go also concentrates the project's most sensitive memory invariants: the state+arena pool is shared across calls via AcquireStateForN / ReleaseStateWithResult, and finalizeStateRelease must call clearStateAliases unconditionally before returning the state to the pool — a regression here would silently corrupt the next computation. The accompanying FAST_DOUBLING.md doc derives the identity, proves it by induction, and explains the three-tier adaptive multiplication pipeline.
tour.languageLesson: Go's `sync.Pool` recycles objects between goroutines to cut GC pressure. The critical invariant is that pooled objects must be reset to a known state before they go back in — otherwise the next consumer sees stale data. fastdoubling.go encodes this discipline: `clearStateAliases` always runs before `statePool.Put`, and the test `TestReleaseState_OverLimit_AliasesCleared` exists specifically to prevent regressions of that ordering.

tour.title: The Doubling Framework and Adaptive Thresholds
tour.description: doubling_framework.go is the generic driver that powers both Fast Doubling and the matrix variants: it walks the bits of N from MSB to bit 0, calling out to a Multiplier strategy for each squaring and multiplication. This is where the choice between schoolbook, Strassen, and FFT actually happens, guided by threshold/manager.go — a single-writer adaptive controller that records per-iteration metrics and shifts the FFT/parallel cutoffs at runtime. The manager's single-writer invariant is not declared in code; introducing a concurrent writer would cause subtle races, which is why CLAUDE.md flags it as a sensitive module.

tour.title: FFT Kernel: Schönhage–Strassen Multiplication
tour.description: For very large N, multiplications dominate. The bigfft package implements Schönhage–Strassen FFT multiplication: fft.go exposes Mul/MulTo and Sqr/SqrTo on big.Int and picks FFT parameters, while fermat.go implements the modular arithmetic in the Fermat ring (mod 2^n+1) that makes the convolution work. fermat.go uses panic-based invariant checks — these are intentional and must propagate; a stray top-level recover would mask post-condition violations. BIGFFT.md walks through the full Schönhage–Strassen pipeline, including the polynomial representation and the amd64 vector intrinsics.

tour.title: FFT Caching and Pooling
tour.description: Raw FFT speed is not enough — the real wins come from not redoing work and not allocating in the hot path. fft_cache.go is an LRU TransformCache that memoizes forward FFT transforms keyed by operand bytes and FFT parameters, giving a documented 15–30% speedup. pool.go centralises four size-classed sync.Pool families (word slice, fermat, nat slice, fermat slice) plus the fftStatePool; releaseWordSlice routes on capacity (not length) so reused buffers always land in the right bucket. Both files carry CLAUDE.md-flagged invariants: the cache must not recycle a backing while a polynomial value still aliases it, and pool routing must respect the cap-based dispatch.
tour.languageLesson: Go's `big.Int` is backed by a `[]Word` slice (`Word` is a `uintptr`-sized digit). Reusing those backing slices via `sync.Pool` is the dominant performance pattern in this codebase — but slice aliasing is subtle: two `big.Int`s sharing a backing array will silently corrupt each other if both are written. The bigfft pools track capacity, not length, because Go slices can be re-sliced to any length up to their capacity, so capacity is the true allocation size.

tour.title: Memory Discipline: Arena and GC Control
tour.description: Across both fibonacci and bigfft, the project follows two complementary memory disciplines. CalculationArena (arena.go) provides slab-style word allocations reused across a single Fibonacci run, falling back to normal allocation when its budget is exceeded. GCController (gc_control.go) goes further for N ≥ 1M: it disables the Go GC entirely during the computation, and guarantees restoration via the panic-safe WithGC wrapper. The deprecated direct Begin/End pair must not be reintroduced — if a panic ever interrupted a computation without restoring GC, the rest of the process would leak memory until exit.
tour.languageLesson: Go's `defer` runs the deferred call when the surrounding function returns — including panics. `WithGC(fn)` exploits this with a `defer End()` so GC is always re-enabled even if `fn` panics mid-calculation. This panic-safe wrapper pattern is idiomatic Go for any resource that must be released exactly once: `sync.Mutex.Lock` / `defer mu.Unlock()`, `os.File.Open` / `defer f.Close()`, and `runtime.GC` toggles all use it.

tour.title: Calibration, Progress, and the TUI
tour.description: The presentation layer turns long-running computations into something observable. calibration.go runs micro-benchmarks ahead of time to pick FFT/Strassen/parallel thresholds for the current host, and persists profiles between runs. progress.go computes total work for Fast Doubling using precomputed powers of 4 (an O(log n) progress model rather than a naive linear one), and observer.go fans events out to subscribers — the production path is Freeze, which snapshots observers atomically. model.go is the Bubble Tea TUI dashboard: its Update router is a pure function by design, per the CLAUDE.md invariant that flags it as a sensitive module.
tour.languageLesson: Bubble Tea models the UI as a pure `Update(msg) -> (model, cmd)` function in the Elm Architecture style. Keeping `Update` pure (no I/O, no shared mutable state) means every state transition is reproducible and testable from the message stream alone — which is exactly why CLAUDE.md treats any side effect leaking into the router as a regression.

tour.title: Tests, Docs, and CI
tour.description: The capstone is the safety net. fibonacci_golden.json is the immutable oracle: every algorithm must produce the same values it lists, and the file cannot be updated without explicit approval. ARCH.md is the top-level architecture reference covering the layers and ten ADRs you've just toured through. The Makefile exposes 37 targets (build, PGO, race-tested tests, benchmarks, lint), and ci.yml replays the most important of them on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS with the race detector on, guarding both correctness and performance across the supported platforms.
tour.languageLesson: Go's race detector (`go test -race`) instruments memory accesses at compile time and reports data races at runtime. It requires CGO, which is why FibGo's CI matrix explicitly sets `CGO_ENABLED=1` on all three OSes. Golden-file testing complements the race detector by guarding the other axis: even if all the concurrency is correct, the algorithm itself must keep producing the same values byte-for-byte against an oracle that was generated by an intentionally independent implementation.
